title: The Golden Rule of Friendship
coreMove: Shift attention outward so the other person leaves the interaction feeling better about themselves, not impressed by you.
sourcePressure: The ch03 source states the Golden Rule of Friendship: if you want people to like you, make them feel good about themselves. It warns against ego, flattery, and obvious performance.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reducing the rule to compliments, agreement, or self-erasure.

sourceAnchors.name: The Golden Rule of Friendship
sourceAnchors.detail: The ch03 sidecar names the rule: if you want people to like you, make them feel good about themselves.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The rule works when the good feeling belongs to them, not when your compliment calls attention to your own cleverness.

sourceAnchors.name: ego override
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says most people fail because ego keeps attention on themselves.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The hard part is not finding praise; it is getting your own need to shine out of the center of the room.

counterintuition: liking is about them, not you

exampleSpecs.domain: a paramedic preceptor debriefing a new EMT after a messy call
exampleSpecs.audience: a senior medic who wants confidence without false praise
exampleSpecs.stakes: a shaky trainee may either learn or shut down
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the preceptor names the exact patient-care decision the trainee handled well before discussing the miss, so the trainee feels competent enough to hear correction
exampleSpecs.firstImage: the ambulance floor smells faintly of antiseptic and rainwater
mustAvoid: empty praise or heroic rescue scene

exampleSpecs.domain: a public library branch manager welcoming a retired engineer to a volunteer tech-help desk
exampleSpecs.audience: a manager who needs the volunteer to feel useful without being patronized
exampleSpecs.stakes: the volunteer may quit if treated like a mascot instead of skilled help
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "You caught what our form misses," Rachel says, pointing to his note before asking for help redesigning the sign-up sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: a climbing gym instructor handling a nervous adult beginner
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor who must keep attention on the beginner instead of performing expertise
exampleSpecs.stakes: one humiliating moment could make the beginner leave the sport
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 7:18 p.m., James chooses to notice the beginner checking her knot correctly instead of showing off a harder move
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a figure-eight knot held in chalky fingers
mustAvoid: bike helmet or sports pep talk shell

exampleSpecs.domain: a city planning facilitator listening to residents angry about a bus-lane proposal
exampleSpecs.audience: a facilitator whose credibility depends on making opponents feel heard
exampleSpecs.stakes: a public meeting can turn hostile before the maps are discussed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the facilitator repeats the resident concerns as practical local knowledge and asks where the map is blind, making critics feel respected without surrendering the proposal
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a roll of traffic maps curling at the corners

exampleSpecs.domain: a software mentor reviewing a junior developer pull request
exampleSpecs.audience: a mentor who must correct without stealing ownership
exampleSpecs.stakes: the junior dev may learn the habit or start hiding mistakes
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you can either showcase your own elegant fix or ask what tradeoff the junior developer was protecting, then name the sound instinct underneath it
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a red test failure beside a small green diff

exampleSpecs.domain: a neighborhood choir director keeping an alto from quitting after missed entrances
exampleSpecs.audience: a director balancing correction with belonging
exampleSpecs.stakes: losing one singer will thin the section before a memorial concert
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes two rehearsals for Juliette to realize the alto returns when feedback starts with the blend she adds, not the mistake she made

skillTargets: distinguish sincere outward attention from flattery
choose responses that leave another person feeling competent or seen

tryThisNowSpec: In your next conversation, ask one follow-up that helps the other person feel competent, useful, or understood, then do not pivot back to your own story.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
